drafts.capability_statement:
Red Cedar Facility Services — Capability Statement
NAICS 561720 | WOSB | EDWOSB | SBA Certified Small Business

Red Cedar Facility Services provides comprehensive janitorial and custodial services to federal healthcare and administrative facilities across Oklahoma. Our directly relevant experience includes housekeeping support at the VA Oklahoma City Health Care System (2023–2025) and custodial services at the Oklahoma City Federal Building (GSA Region 7), giving us proven familiarity with VA protocols, federal security requirements, and multi-site operations in the Oklahoma City metro area.

Our 38 W-2 employees support two-shift daily coverage (6:00 am–2:30 pm and 3:00 pm–11:30 pm) across multiple locations without reliance on subcontractors for core labor. Supervisors hold OSHA 30 certifications, enabling contractor-furnished training aligned to 29 CFR 1910 standards within required timeframes. Our CIMS-GB certification demonstrates adherence to industry quality benchmarks, and our CMMS-based QC inspection program provides the documented daily and monthly reporting discipline required for RME closet logs and COR submissions.

We deploy EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectants and maintain a green cleaning program consistent with VA infection control requirements, including immediate response to blood and body fluid incidents and high-touch surface disinfection. Floor care capabilities include strip, scrub, burnish, wax, and carpet extraction. Window cleaning is a listed core service.

Red Cedar is enrolled in e-Verify and has performed under VA electronic invoicing requirements (VAAR 852.232-72) on prior contracts.

Point of Contact: [Owner Name] | [Phone] | [Email]
questions_for_co: SDVOSB eligibility — The solicitation states award shall be made only to a certified SDVOSB listed in the SBA certification database [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-5f011c82]. Is there any possibility the set-aside designation will be amended to unrestricted or to a different socioeconomic category before proposal due date, or is SDVOSB certification a firm, non-waivable condition of award?

Wage determination applicability — The solicitation references a minimum wage rate of $13.65 per hour through December 31, 2026 [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-6c461140]. Which specific WD number and revision applies to this contract, and does a separate rate apply for the Lawton and Stillwater locations given their different counties?

Uniform and equipment reimbursement — The wage determination requires reimbursement to employees for cleaning and maintenance of required uniforms [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-34ebd09c]. Can the Contracting Officer confirm the exact uniform specification and whether a government-furnished uniform allowance is included, or whether the cost must be embedded in the offeror's price?

PIV / identification card incident reporting — The solicitation requires an incident report to the Program Manager within 48 hours of a lost or stolen PIV card, and a police report copy within 48 hours of its availability [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-821580f5; ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-708b6321]. Is there a government-provided incident report template, and who is the designated Program Manager for this contract?

RME closet SOP access — The solicitation requires cleaning in accordance with facility-established SOPs for RME closets [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-885aa7a2]. Will the government provide copies of the applicable SOPs prior to contract award, or only at the post-award kickoff, and will offerors have an opportunity to review them during site visit?

Paid sick leave compliance — The solicitation incorporates Executive Order 13706 requiring 1 hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked, up to 56 hours annually [ccf5e965-42587fc3-p1-53b80f7e]. Does the government require offerors to submit a written paid sick leave policy with their proposal, or is a certification of compliance sufficient?

reader.scope_summary: The government is buying janitorial services covering all interior spaces at the Oklahoma City Main VA Medical Center, Lawton Main Clinic, Lawton North Clinic, and Stillwater CBOC, with the contractor providing all management, supervision, and labor. Services include daily basic cleaning (floors, trash, restrooms, glass, dusting, stairwells, elevators, RME closets) as well as periodic intensive floor maintenance, carpet cleaning, and disinfection using EPA-registered hospital-grade products. Work is performed Monday through Friday across two shifts (6:00am–2:30pm and 3:00pm–11:30pm), with on-site personnel presence required throughout each shift.
